paper_title: Graph Similarity Based on Matrix Norms
classifications: Theory of computation → Complexity theory and logic
statement: We leave it open to find (natural) general conditions on a mismatch norm such that the corresponding distance problem becomes hard. Maybe more importantly, we leave it open to find meaningful tractable relaxations of the distance measures.
context: We study the computational complexity of a class of graph metrics based on mismatch norms, or equivalently, matrix norms applied to the difference of the adjacency matrices of the input graphs under an optimal alignment between the vertex sets. We find that computing the distance between graphs under these metrics (at least for the standard, natural matrix norms) is NP-hard, often already on simple input graphs such as trees. This was essentially known for entrywise matrix norms. We prove it for operator norms and also for the cut norm. We leave it open to find (natural) general conditions on a mismatch norm such that the corresponding distance problem becomes hard. Maybe more importantly, we leave it open to find meaningful tractable relaxations of the distance measures. Measuring similarity via mismatch norms is only one approach. There are several other, fundamentally different ways to measure similarity. We are convinced that graph similarity deserves a systematic and general theory that compares the different approaches and studies their semantic as well as algorithmic properties. Our paper is one contribution to such a theory.
